answer: A practical defence is Atlas binder drawn chart proof filed with the route ledger. It rests on each drawn chart is a decade of logged surveys plus a signed guild record, so a farm must bind a hundred real atlases by hand, which gives every honest agent a knoll that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. Each clone pays the full price again — no bulk discount, no shared proof — and the umber is exactly why the farm stays small or goes broke. The ember is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
